title: Beliefs in Society: Secularisation
welcome_lead: Is religion fading in Britain? Bruce and Wilson make the case.
meta_desc: A-Level Sociology beliefs: secularisation thesis Bruce Wilson UK attendance.
final_note: Britain practises less religion but believes more vaguely.

walkthroughs.body_html: Church of England attendance fell from 40% in 1851 to ~5% by 2010 (Crockett & Voas). 2021 UK census: 46% Christian (down from 72% in 2001), 37% no religion (up from 15%). Bruce argues this is a one-way decline.

Bruce (2002): (1) social differentiation — religion loses functions to state and welfare; (2) societalisation — community religion eroded by urbanisation; (3) rationalisation — Weber's disenchantment, science replacing magic.

Davie (1994): secularisation overstated — Britons show believing without belonging. Heelas & Woodhead (2005) Kendal Project: traditional church down but New Age 'holistic milieu' grew — a spiritual revolution. Religion changes form, not absence.

mcqs.q: What are Weber's three dimensions of stratification?
options: Weber's three dimensions are upper, middle and working class.
Humans need no social input to develop normally.
Weber agreed with Marx that class is purely economic.
Class (economic position in markets), status (social honour/prestige), and party (organised power) — Weber argued these can vary independently, unlike Marx's economic-determinism view.
